handoff: F1 blocking: round.migrate not crash-safe (partial move → resolver reads empty round, story looks not started/corrupt, never resumes); F2 minor: AC3 fixture lacks logs/ and slice folder

findings.title: A migration that stops halfway leaves a record the resolver misreads (story looks not started or corrupt), and nothing resumes it
findings.detail:
roundMigrate first runs mkdirSync(to), then moves the entries one at a time in sorted order (evidence, logs, receipts, state.json, workflow.yaml), and commits only at the end. git.move uses `must` (packages/adapters/src/git/index.ts:304) and throws on any git failure, for example an index.lock held by the agent's own git in the same worktree. A crash or kill between the steps can do the same. After a partial move, currentRound() (packages/store/src/paths.ts) finds rounds/01-<wf>/ and unitDir() resolves the story there. (a) If state.json has not moved yet, the round folder has no state, so observe reports state null: the story looks not started, su.record is no longer 'runs/_story', and round.migrate never fires again. startDir would also write a fresh record there. (b) If state.json moved but workflow.yaml did not, decideUnit emits mark_corrupt unit.workflow_missing. Both cases are the plan's named risk ('a missed reader sees an empty folder and treats the story as not started') and break S5's rule that state is the commit point. Trace: run roundMigrate with git.move throwing on the 4th entry, then observe; the story unit has state null and record runs/_story/rounds/01-<wf>.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Make the move resumable. While runs/_story/state.json still exists, the resolver (currentRound/unitDir and isFlatStoryRecord) should treat the record as flat, so decide emits round.migrate again and the next run moves whatever is left. In roundMigrate, move state.json last (after workflow.yaml) and skip entries already at the target. Add a test that stops the move partway (an injected git.move failure), then ticks and expects round.migrate to finish the move with the state intact.

findings.title: AC3's flat fixture has no logs/, and 'slice folders are untouched' is not asserted
findings.detail:
AC3: 'state at implement, receipts, logs, evidence directly under runs/_story/ … Slice folders are untouched.' The duo workflow has no check step, so the flat record has no logs/ folder. Logs are the entry most likely to be untracked or ignored, which sends them down roundMigrate's plain-move fallback, and that path is never exercised. The test also has no slice folder to show that it survives the move.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: In the setup, add an untracked runs/_story/logs/<id>.log and a sibling runs/01-x/ folder. Assert that the log ends up in rounds/01-duo/logs/ and that the slice folder is byte-for-byte unchanged.
